recipes.name: Vegetarian Enchilada Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (4 ounce) can diced green chile peppers

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees (175 degrees C). Lightly oil a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine beans, garlic, onion, chile peppers, jalapeño pepper, and tempeh in a medium bowl. Pour enchilada sauce into a shallow bowl.

Dip three tortillas in enchilada sauce, and place them in the prepared baking dish. Be sure to cover bottom of the dish as completely as possible. Place 1/2 of the bean mixture on top of the tortillas, and repeat. Drizzle remaining sauce over the casserole, and sprinkle with olives and shredded cheese.
Cover, and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover, and continue baking for an additional 15 minutes, or until the casserole is bubbling and the cheese is melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Enchilada Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This vegetarian enchilada casserole has layers of tortillas with enchilada sauce loaded with black beans, spicy peppers, tempeh, and lots of cheese.

review.reviewBody: Using previous reviews (thank you!)I eliminated the pepper and tempeh, added 1+ cup corn and 1+ cup diced tomatoes to the bean mixture, and refrigerated the casserole overnight. Baked it 40 minutes + 15 minutes and it was GREAT! Served to multi-generational group and all liked it!

Fantastic! I followed the recipe with the following modifications or additions. I didn't want to dice a jalapeno myself, so I used canned jalapeno. I tore up the corn tortillas in quarters so it would be easier to dish up and went with Mexican blend cheese. Minor, minor changes. And finally I added about 2 tbsp chipotle seasoning, 1 tsp garlic pepper, and 1/2 tsp chili powder. It was delicious, spicy, and awesomely flavorful! I was a bit afraid of the tempeh, but it was good. My husband had no idea there was soy in there until I told him. I recommend using a large mixing bowl to stir it all together. A medium bowl wasn't quite big enough. I love the recipe and will make it again soon. I already added it to my hard copy recipe book. This is a keeper! It was such a nice change not to have to precook meat for a dish like this. We didn't miss it.

Love this recipe! I just tried it for my first time last night and I have to say thank you for posting this! I'm even eating it for lunch today. My boyfriend and I are huge fans of Mexican/Southwest recipes and I recently went vegetarian, so this dish appealed to both of us. I did make a few adjustments. I tore apart the corn tortillas and layered them, then poured green enchilada sauce on top instead of dipping them. I also did three layers (tortillas, enchilada sauce, bean mix, tortillas, enchilada sauce, bean mix, tortillas, enchilada sauce, cheese). I sauteed the onions (cut in long halfmoon slices), garlic, green chilies (I doubled them), and jalapeno (used a can of diced jalapenos, which tripled the serving size, but WILL NOT next time, way too spicy!!!) in a little olive oil before. I also added a 15 oz can of pinto beans to the mixture. Served with salsa and sour cream. So yummy!

Made a vegan version (thanks for the recipe). Added one can of pinto and one can of black beans each. Added two bags of Morning Star beefless crumbles, substituted with one bag each of Go Veggie dairy-free cheddar and mozzarella cheeses, two boxes of El Paso Spanish-style rice, and sautéed the onion alone then added the beefless crumbes to the onions. Browned with two packets of taco seasoning. Added the fresh garlic to the beefless crumbles at the end of cooking. Also added one can of corn. Served with dairy-free sour cream and voila Bon appetite!

This turned to be a great casserole, considering some modifications made based on ingredients I had on hand. Like other reviewers, I used red enchilada sauce. Instead of tempeh, I substituted vegetarian ground "meat" crumbles. This worked well, and I think ground turkey or beef would be just as good for non-vegetarians. I added more cheese to the first layer in addition to the top of the casserole, and finally, used a can of diced jalapeños instead of green chiles, which definitely added some heat!

Before making this casserole, I'd only put tempeh in stir fries. I added a little chile powder, cilantro, oregano, and lime juice to the mixture. I also sauteed the onion, jalapeño and tempeh a bit before adding it all to the mix. Good stuff, and I'll almost definitely make it again.

Great! I added a few more tortillas to ensure there was no gap between the layers. I added a can of corn to the mixture, sautéed the onions before adding, and also added taco seasoning mix to the mixture! So great!

I used this as a basic recipe and changed according to our families tastes. I cut my corn tortillas into strips and used them like lasagna noodles. I used seasoned ground meat instead of Tempeh. Added a layer of roasted red peppers and a layer of sour cream mixed with green chillis and jalapenos. Added crushed tortilla chips to the top for crunch. Cooked according to the directions and let sit for about 15 minutes after I took out of the oven. Served with Guacamole and sour cream. Delicious! Will definitely add to my recipe box for the future.

Our family loved this but I made a number of changes based of previous reviews. As suggested, I soaked my corn tortillas in red enchilada sauce while I prepared everything else. My kids are young and don't like spicy stuff and my husband doesn't like onions. I also had no clue what tempeh was. So, instead I used 1 can of corn, 1 can of refried black beans, 1 cup of diced tomatoes, and 1 red pepper. I took the garlic, red pepper, corn and tomatoes and heated them in a skillet with 1 Tbsp olive oil. I added 1 tsp each of chili powder, cumin, and salt. I then mixed this in with the refried beans and black beans and layered as directed in the recipe. With these modifications it turned out great for our family and I'll definitely be making it again.

I didn't like it. The onions were way too strong. Sautéing them first would probably help. I oiled the pan but it still stuck to the bottom. It was also a little dry -- similar recipes usually call for 2 cans of sauce instead of 1.

I have made it twice, first time with tempeh and red sauce, no jalapeno and added can of corn. I did two layers of bean mixture and tortillas. It came out fine. Our normal enchilada recipe uses green sauce and chicken, so next time I cut and cooked up two boneless, skinless chicken breast with garlic, red onions and spices. then used green enchilada sauce and added the can of corn and made two layers of bean sauce and 3 layers of corn tortillas (bottom, middle and top) Turned out amazing.

I absolutely loved this recipe!!! It is easy, great enchilada flavor, stores well in the fridge and gets better over time! Really can't ask for more :) The one thing I did was make some Spanish rice to mix in when I reheated it. It blended well with the casserole.
My family loved this. I think the only changes I made was to use poblano peppers instead of jalapenos and I used ground un-beef instead of tempeh. They are requesting it again.
A keeper. This dish is delicious and warming in a cold winters night.
Loved this dish. Made some minor changes. I did not use a jalapeno pepper (husband does not like any spicy hot) but used a yellow pepper. Also I used about 24 oz of enchilada sauce.
I substituted Chicked for the tofu mix. Also added less black olives. It turned out really well.

Made one for me and one for a friend, I use ground turkey with taco mix and table spoon of sriracha sauce, no jalapeños, extra diced green chilies red sauce, quest cheese in side and cheddar for top! Soooo good!

The 1st time I made this there was not enough to feed my family of 4. I made it according to the recipe except I had no Tempeh. Everyone loved it, just not enough. I doubled the recipe the next time I made it and served with chips and salsa, everyone loved it.

Tasted great (I doubled the recipe and made 4 layers packed tight!) but next time around I will sweat the onions first. They didn't really cook in the casserole and they were slightly too much (just slightly). It was so good though. Like eating loaded nachos with a fork!!
I made it with Beyond Beef and vegan cheese. It is delicious! We have been eating this every few nights.
